heroHeadline: June 2: PLA 7 Sorties All SW ADIZ, Zero Median Crossings (First Since May 31) — 8 PLAN Vessels + 5 Ships; Computex 2026 Opens in Taipei: Intel CEO + Nvidia Jensen Huang Taiwan Investment Expansion; TSMC Plans 15% 3nm Price Hike
heroSubtitle: On June 2, 2026, Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 7 PLA aircraft sorties with all entering the southwestern ADIZ but NONE crossing the Taiwan Strait median line — the first zero-crossing day since May 31's HIMARS deadline-day pullback, representing a slight air de-escalation from June 1's 8 sorties (2 crossing SW/E ADIZ). Eight PLAN vessels and 5 official ships operated around Taiwan, a marginal uptick in naval presence from June 1's 7+4 configuration. The extended May–June sortie sequence reads: 4→29→1→2→1→0→22→12→8→12→7→9→2→3→15→6→7→13→24→7→6→16→4→9→26→10→9→10→16→1→8→7. On the same day, Computex 2026 opened in Taipei: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan arrived for TSMC meetings; Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced a major expansion of Nvidia's investment in Taiwan, driving TSMC shares up ~4.8%; and TSMC is reported to be planning a 15% price increase on 3nm process services in H2 2026 amid AI demand surge from Nvidia, AMD, Google, and AWS — underscoring Taiwan's irreplaceable position in global AI supply chains even as PLA pressure continues. Taiwan's HIMARS NT$800M down payment was confirmed met on May 31 with Executive Yuan emergency reserve backstop; the NT$8.81B FY2026 procurement budget passed without opposition May 29. US FMS pause for Operation Epic Fury (Iran) remains active; $14B PAC-3/NASAMS package remains 'in abeyance' (Trump).
